title: If someone calls claiming your grandchild is in jail
prompt: A weeping caller says your grandchild was arrested and needs bail money wired secretly. Put these steps in order:
steps: Hang up the call to break their emotional panic and pressure.
Call your grandchild directly on their normal cell phone number.
If they don't answer, call their parents or another relative to check.
Never wire money or send gift cards to a stranger claiming to be a lawyer or police officer.
whyFirstStepMatters: Hanging up breaks the artificial panic. Scammers rely on keeping you on the line so you cannot speak to your family and discover the truth.
explanation: Family emergency scams succeed by keeping grandparents in a state of terror. Hanging up and calling your grandchild directly almost always reveals they are safe at school or work.
takeaways: Always hang up and call your relative directly.
Never let panic rush you into sending money.

title: Text claiming your nephew is in the emergency room

segments.text: URGENT NOTICE: This is Nurse Martinez at the trauma center.
Your nephew Alex was brought into the emergency room following a serious car accident and requires immediate care.

flag.reason: Scammers fabricate extreme bodily injury to trigger panic and bypass your normal caution.

segments.text: The hospital requires an immediate medical deposit of $2,400 before the surgical suite can be opened.

flag.reason: Emergency rooms in the United States treat life-threatening injuries immediately and never demand text payment before operating.

segments.text: Send the funds via digital transfer to billing@county-trauma-care.org right now. Do not call his mother as she is not at home.

flag.reason: Telling you not to call family members is a deliberate tactic to keep you isolated from the truth.

explanation: No legitimate emergency medical facility demands cash transfers or app payments over SMS before treating emergency patients. Always call your family member or their immediate relatives on their real phone numbers.
takeaways: Hospitals never demand digital transfers by text before surgery.
Call family directly on their known numbers to verify emergencies.
